speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the rash on your scalp and forehead, specifically when it started and if it is itchy or painful?

text: My parents say the rash has been there for several weeks and looks red with greasy yellow scales. They mention it gets worse in cold weather, but it doesn't seem to bother me or cause any pain. speaker: Doctor
text:
It appears there is a significant discrepancy between the clinical presentation of seborrheic dermatitis and the offline records citing a rare Z-Syndrome. I must rely on the visible physical signs and history rather than the contradictory administrative data. Given the classic appearance of red, greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead that worsen in cold weather, I am proceeding with the clinical diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic Dermatitis
